config.title: Berlin Weekly Markets - FAQ
config.subtitle: Which market runs on which day, how late you can turn up, and why Sunday is the one day that has none.

items.q: What day are the markets in Berlin?
items.a: **Every day except Sunday, but a different set each day.** Saturday is the biggest with nine markets worth crossing the city for. Wednesday is the classic morning, with Winterfeldtplatz 08:00 to 14:00 and Karl-August-Platz 08:00 to 13:00. Thursday has the widest spread and the latest hours. Tuesday and Friday belong to the Maybachufer Turkish market, 11:00 to 18:30. Monday has only Markthalle Neun, 12:00 to 18:00. On a Sunday no weekly food market trades at all.

items.q: What time do Berlin markets close?
items.a: **Earlier than most visitors expect.** The classic produce squares finish between 13:00 and 16:00: Karl-August-Platz at 13:00 on a Wednesday, Winterfeldtplatz at 14:00 on a Wednesday and 16:00 on a Saturday, Boxhagener Platz at 15:30. The afternoon markets run later, with Maybachufer to 18:30 and Arkonaplatz and the Kollwitzplatz organic market to 19:00. Street Food Thursday inside Markthalle Neun is the latest of all at 22:00.

items.q: Which is the best market in Berlin for a visitor?
items.a: **Winterfeldtplatz on a Saturday if you want the full version, Maybachufer if your day starts late.** Winterfeldtplatz in Schöneberg is the biggest and best known weekly market in the city and runs 08:00 to 16:00 on a Saturday, which is the longest a produce square trades all week. If you are only free in the afternoon, the Turkish market at Maybachufer in Neukölln does not open until 11:00 and trades to 18:30 on Tuesdays and Fridays.

items.q: Is there a market in Berlin on a Sunday?
items.a: **Not a food market, no.** Every weekly market in Berlin is closed on a Sunday, and Markthalle Neun is closed as well. What Sunday does have is the flea markets, and they are a proper day out: Mauerpark in Prenzlauer Berg and the Trödelmarkt on Boxhagener Platz in Friedrichshain both run on Sundays.

items.q: Can you pay by card at Berlin markets?
items.a: **Bring cash.** Market stalls are the most reliably cash-only corner of Berlin. Some traders now take cards and plenty still do not, and there is rarely a cash machine on the square itself. Take out what you need before you go, and bring your own bag: shops and stalls in Germany charge for plastic bags when they have them at all.

items.q: Which Berlin market is closest to the city centre?
items.a: **Hackescher Markt in Mitte.** It sets up on the square in front of the S-Bahn station on Thursdays 09:00 to 18:00 and Saturdays 10:00 to 18:00, with Brandenburg fruit and vegetables, cheese, fish rolls, lahmacun and baked potatoes. It is also the square where my walking tour finishes, so on those two days you can eat lunch at the stalls without moving.

items.q: Do Berlin markets open on public holidays?
items.a: **No, and that catches people out.** German public holidays fall on weekdays, and the squares simply do not open on them. Heavy rain also shortens the day, because individual traders pack down an hour or two early on the smaller squares. Check the date before you build a morning around a market.
